message.content: Lions mate during a brief but intense courtship period that typically lasts only a few days. When a male approaches a female’s pride, he will first scent-mark her territory with urine and feces to signal his presence and dominance. If the female is receptive, she will allow him to approach and may even display submissive postures such as lying on her side or rolling onto her back. Once close enough, the male will mount the female from behind and they will copulate for a short time—usually less than a minute. After mating, the male may stay nearby to guard the female against other males, ensuring his paternity. This entire process is driven by hormonal cues and social signals within the pride.
